candidate.title: JBP1-seq
candidate.scope: The JBP1-seq middle row of the assigned Illumina poster: transposome/Nextera-based tagmentation of 5hmC-containing genomic DNA, T4-βGT glucosylation, JBP1 magnetic-bead enrichment and PCR to a DNA library. JBP1-seq expands to J-binding protein 1 sequencing. The matching collection page is secondary catalogue clarification, and Cui et al. (2014) is inspected at metadata and abstract level only. Neighboring T-WGBS and Aba-seq rows, clipped text from other rows and the cropped chemical-legend context are not connected alternatives of this target. The endpoint is prepared DNA; sequencing and computational processing are not depicted operations.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Transposomes act on the hydroxymethylated genomic DNA to fragment it and add terminal adapter sequences. The output retains the genomic inserts and their depicted 5hmC residues. The transposome icons represent the acting reagent complexes, not a separate workflow branch.
operations.mechanism: Transposome-mediated tagmentation; the primary abstract identifies the library construction as Nextera-based. No internal transposome preparation or unshown repair sequence is reconstructed.
operations.information_effect: Genomic sequence carrying 5hmC becomes divided into adapter-bearing fragments that can subsequently be selected and amplified.

operations.label: T4-βGT
operations.description: T4-βGT acts on 5hmC residues in the tagmented adapter-bearing fragments to produce glucosylated 5hmC. Blue flags appear at the residue symbols while the drawn DNA and terminal adapters continue through the operation.
operations.mechanism: T4 β-glucosyltransferase-mediated glucosylation of 5hmC; T4-βGT is the enzyme reagent, not the material converted into DNA.
operations.information_effect: The pre-existing 5hmC positions acquire the glucosylated modification recognized by the subsequent JBP1 capture step.
